title: Short Stuff: Oedipus Complex
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Oedipus complex. Josh and Chuck explain Freud's theory that young children unconsciously desire the opposite-sex parent and feel rivalry toward the same-sex parent, contrast it with the Greek myth of Oedipus, and recount Freud's case of "Little Hans" and his extension of the idea to girls (with the Electra complex attributed to Carl Jung). They note Freud's theories were largely conjecture and are mostly discredited, discuss a 2009 Proceedings of the Royal Society B paper on facial similarity between men's wives and mothers that other scientists challenged, and mention a 1980s rat study and attachment theory as alternatives.

entities.name: Proceedings of the Royal Society B

segments.title: Opening banter on Freud
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Short Stuff episode and joke about laying blame on Sigmund Freud, saying he was an innovative thinker rather than a rigorous scientist.

segments.title: Freud's Oedipus complex and the Greek myth
segments.summary: Josh explains Freud's observation that young children are hostile toward one parent and attached to the other, and that this became the Oedipus complex, which he based on conjecture. Chuck summarizes the Greek myth of Oedipus, who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother, and Josh notes the myth was about fate rather than gore.

segments.title: Definitions of the Oedipus complex
segments.summary: Chuck reads the Simply Psychology definition of the phallic stage (ages three to six) with unconscious desire for the opposite-sex parent and jealousy toward the same-sex parent. Josh offers a Britannica definition describing sexual desire for the opposite-sex parent and rivalry with the same-sex parent as a crucial developmental stage.

segments.title: Little Hans case study
segments.summary: Chuck describes Freud's case study of a four-year-old, Little Hans, who feared horses after seeing a horse-drawn cart collapse. Josh recounts Freud's interpretation that the fear reflected hostility toward his father and fear of castration, and jokes about the reaction.

segments.title: Girls, Electra complex, and consequences of non-resolution
segments.summary: Josh says Freud applied the Oedipal idea to girls, with penis envy in place of castration anxiety, and notes Carl Jung coined the name Electra complex. Chuck explains Freud's claim that failing to resolve the complex would prevent normal sexual maturity, and Josh says Freud linked incomplete development to homosexuality, a view that is discredited.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Brief break before the discussion resumes.

segments.title: Is Freud's theory correct?
segments.summary: Chuck says most psychologists consider Freud's theories discredited though some support remains. Josh describes a 2009 Proceedings of the Royal Society B paper claiming men's wives resemble their mothers, which other scientists challenged after reviewing the data.

segments.title: Alternative explanations and rat study
segments.summary: Chuck suggests people may partner with parents who were admirable, and Josh suggests people may seek partners resembling their parents' worst traits. Josh mentions a 1980s rat study claiming support for the complex, and says attachment theory offers less creepy explanations of child development.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close out the episode and a sponsor/production credit is read.
